answer: A farm cannot tell which of its aliases will be pulled, so it carries the risk on every one of them rather than on a few. Because the falcon sample is drawn from the ferrous beacon, the wharf audit makes public the selection was not made by the operator, and the probation is recorded per key. A random 13% of submissions is pulled for manual review, and a reviewer's finding of fabrication voids the answer and starts a probation. That is 16 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
